chunks: Al-Husayn from Fadalah from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Ibrahim ibn Maymun from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who leads women in prayer and there is no man with them in the obligatory prayer, he said: 'Yes, and if there is a boy with him, let him stand beside him.'
ai.seo_question: Can a man lead women in prayer if there are no other men present?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the permissibility of a man leading women in congregational prayer (*fard*) when no other adult male is available. The ruling emphasizes that the presence of even a young boy (*sabi*) standing beside the Imam is sufficient to validate the prayer structure, reflecting the Shia juristic view on the flexibility of *imamah* in mixed-gender settings under specific conditions.
